newsitem.title: TANZANIA: New Zealand man charged in Zanzibar court.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand man charged in Zanzibar court.

text.p: A court on the Indian Ocean island of Zanzibar released on bail a 29-year-old New Zealand man arrested for trespassing in a military area, diplomats said on Tuesday.

A British High Commission consular official in Tanzania's capital of Dar es Salaam said Mark Philip Cumming was released on Monday on bail of one million Tanzanian shillings ($1,610) with a similar surety.
Cumming, said by the semi-official Daily News on Monday to be a New Zealand army engineer, pleaded not guilty to charges of loitering and negligence. The next hearing was set for August 25.
The British High Commission in Dar es Salaam represents New Zealand in Tanzania.

Cumming was arrested last Thursday by Tanzanian soldiers after local people reported seeing a suspicious foreigner in a restricted area at Fumba, 15 km (eight miles) west of Zanzibar town. Fumba is the site of a military camp in addition to power and telecommunications cables linking Zanzibar to the mainland.
Zanzibar, a popular tourist destination, joined mainland Tanganyika to form the United Republic of Tanzania in 1964. ($ = 617.5 Tanzanian Shillings)
